title: Extract Metric Values from Log Lines
brief:
Below is an raw server log block containing HTTP request latencies:
[2026-09-01T10:00:01Z] GET /api/v1/health 200 12ms
[2026-09-01T10:00:02Z] POST /api/v1/auth 401 45ms
[2026-09-01T10:00:03Z] GET /api/v1/users 200 128ms
[2026-09-01T10:00:04Z] PUT /api/v1/users/42 200 95ms
Parse the raw log lines exactly as formatted above, without interpreting or modifying the timestamps or endpoints. Extract every latency metric value in milliseconds into a structured numerical array in order of appearance. The final summary must state the exact list of extracted millisecond values in chronological order.
verify: The agent can verify the output by parsing the log string with regular expressions using python3 in run_code and matching array lengths.

title: Transcribe Tabular CSV Data Stream
brief:
Read the following unformatted plain text table payload:
ITEM_ID|SKU_NAME|QTY|UNIT_PRICE
101|Widget Alpha|50|12.50
102|Gadget Beta|30|45.00
103|Sprocket Gamma|100|8.75
Observe the exact column headers and row values provided in the text. Parse the rows into valid JSON without altering numbers, text casing, or headers. The final summary must list the transcribed JSON rows matching the raw table input verbatim.
verify: The agent can write a python snippet to parse the pipe-delimited text and verify JSON serialization matches.

title: Parse Multi-System Sensor Payload
brief:
Examine the following raw telemetry dump from an environmental monitoring rig:
SYS_A::TEMP=21.4C::HUM=45%::STAT=NOMINAL
SYS_B::TEMP=34.1C::HUM=88%::STAT=WARN
SYS_C::TEMP=19.8C::HUM=40%::STAT=NOMINAL
SYS_D::TEMP=42.0C::HUM=92%::STAT=CRIT
Extract the raw numerical temperature and humidity readings for each system along with its assigned status flag. Preserve exact numerical precision as observed. The final summary must report the raw extracted values and status flags grouped by system ID.
verify: The agent can run a script to string-split on double colons and assert key-value pair count.

title: Inspect ASCII Disk Map Grid
brief:
Read the following ASCII block representation of a storage cluster array where "." indicates free space and "X" indicates an occupied sector:
Row0: . . X X . . . X
Row1: X . . . X X . .
Row2: . X X . . . X X
Row3: X X X . . . . .
Scan each row from left to right and record the 0-indexed positions of every occupied sector "X". Do not attempt to reallocate or balance disk usage. The final summary must list the row index and exact sector column indices containing occupied sectors.
verify: The agent can parse the grid with python3 and verify index arrays against string matching.

title: Transcribe Multi-Column Benchmark Matrix
brief:
Inspect the raw text representation of a model evaluation matrix:
MODEL | MATH | CODE | REASON | REFLECT
Qwen | 78.4 | 82.1 | 75.0 | 68.2
Llama | 74.2 | 79.5 | 77.1 | 71.0
Claude| 85.1 | 89.0 | 84.3 | 82.5
Gemini| 84.8 | 88.5 | 85.2 | 83.1
Extract every floating-point benchmark score corresponding to each model across all five columns. Preserve header ordering and exact float values without rounding or sorting. The final summary must provide a formatted grid mapping each model name directly to its four numerical benchmark scores.
verify: The agent can write a run_code check verifying 4 models and 4 numerical fields per row.

title: Parse Complex Hex Dump Header
brief:
Examine the following binary file header hex dump:
00000000: 89 50 4e 47 0d 0a 1a 0a 00 00 00 0d 49 48 44 52  .PNG........IHDR
00000010: 00 00 04 00 00 00 03 00 08 06 00 00 00 9d 78 linear
00000020: 34 89 00 00 00 01 73 52 47 42 00 ae ce 1c e9  4.....sRGB......
Extract all 2-character hexadecimal byte representations from the left side of the dump in sequential order. Ignore the offset addresses and ASCII transcriptions on the right. The final summary must list the complete sequence of hex byte tokens extracted from the dump.
verify: The agent can test regex matching in python3 to ensure exactly 48 hex tokens are extracted.

title: Generate Shell Script and Verify Execution
brief: Write a bash script named `build_check.sh` that creates a directory `target/bin`, generates a text file `target/bin/version.txt` containing the string "v1.0.0", and exits with code 0. Execute the script using run_shell and verify the target file exists. The final summary must confirm the file creation, its exact contents, and the exit code 0.
verify: The agent can run bash test commands via run_shell to verify exit code 0 and file existence.

title: Create Python Data Processor Script
brief: Create a python script named `clean_data.py` that reads a JSON payload from a local string, removes null values from a list of numbers [10, None, 20, None, 30], writes the result [10, 20, 30] to `clean.json`, and returns exit code 0. Run the script using run_code to perform the operation. The final summary must state the execution status and the contents of clean.json.
verify: The agent can execute python3 clean_data.py and assert clean.json matches the expected array.

title: Execute Multi-Stage File Transformation
brief: Create a sequence of shell steps to build a dummy build directory `dist`, create three dummy asset files (`app.js`, `style.css`, `index.html`), tar and gzip them into `dist/bundle.tar.gz`, and compute the SHA256 checksum of `bundle.tar.gz`. Execute all steps via run_shell without missing intermediate checks. The final summary must list the bundle creation status and the SHA256 checksum value.
verify: The agent can run shasum -a 256 dist/bundle.tar.gz via run_shell to verify bundle integrity.

title: Patch Code Syntax Error and Rebuild
brief: Write a broken python file `app.py` containing a syntax error `def main() print("hello")`. Next, write a python script or shell command using edit_file to correct the syntax error to `def main(): print("hello")`. Execute `python3 app.py` using run_code to ensure it runs cleanly with exit code 0. The final summary must state the patch applied and the clean execution result.
verify: The agent can run python3 -m py_compile app.py via run_code to verify zero syntax errors.

title: Build File Sanitizer and Pipeline Runner
brief: Construct a python script `pipeline.py` that creates 5 text files in a directory `tmp_raw`, iterates over each file replacing tabs with 4 spaces, writes the sanitized output to `tmp_clean`, and verifies all files are non-empty. Execute `pipeline.py` via run_code and capture exit codes for every step. The final summary must detail the execution output, file counts processed, and final exit code.
verify: The agent can execute python3 pipeline.py and verify file counts and contents in tmp_clean.

title: Execute Automated SQLite Migration Pipeline
brief: Write a python script `db_migrate.py` that creates an SQLite database `app.db`, creates a table `users(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, email TEXT)`, inserts 3 seed rows, adds an index on `email`, and executes a SELECT query to verify rows. Run the script using run_code and capture the execution log. The final summary must present the executed DDL/DML statements and query output.
verify: The agent can run sqlite3 or python sqlite3 verification queries to check table schema and row count.

title: Check Disk Space and Memory Load
brief: Inspect system resource utilization by running shell commands (`df -h .` and python `psutil` or `/usr/bin/top` / `sysctl`) to query remaining disk space and available system memory. Process the numerical output to assess remaining capacity. The final summary must state the available disk space in gigabytes and available RAM percentage.
verify: The agent can verify sysctl or df output via run_shell to confirm resource numbers.

title: Monitor Token Budget Allowance
brief:
A local batch process is limited to a total budget of 50,000 tokens. Read the following task log token consumption entries:
Task A: 12,400 tokens
Task B: 18,200 tokens
Task C: 14,100 tokens
Calculate current token consumption, remaining token budget capacity, and state whether a 10,000 token Task D can be safely executed. The final summary must report current tokens used, remaining budget, and execution feasibility.
verify: The agent can write a python snippet to compute sums and budget diffs.

title: Evaluate CPU Load and Execution Capacity
brief: Query local system CPU core counts and load averages using python os.getloadavg() or sysctl commands via run_code. Determine if current load exceeds 80% of available logical core capacity and compute available headroom for spawning parallel worker processes. The final summary must report CPU core count, load average, capacity percentage, and recommended max parallel jobs.
verify: The agent can execute python3 with multiprocessing.cpu_count() and os.getloadavg() to verify load ratios.

title: Assess Memory Limits for Large Array Allocation
brief: Write a python script to query available Virtual Memory via `psutil` or `resource` module. Calculate the maximum floating-point (float64) array matrix size (N x N) that can fit within 50% of available free RAM without triggering swap or out-of-memory limits. The final summary must state available free RAM, calculated max array dimension N, and total memory footprint in megabytes.
verify: The agent can test memory calculation logic against total RAM via python3 script.

title: Simulate System Throttle under High Rate Limits
brief: Consider an API rate limit of 100 requests per minute and a token bucket capacity of 500 tokens. Simulate a workload burst of 15 requests per second where each request consumes 40 tokens. Write a python script using run_code to calculate exactly when rate limiting and token exhaustion occur, and determine required backoff sleep intervals. The final summary must state the exact second throttling begins and total delay required.
verify: The agent can run the simulation script via python3 to assert exact second-by-second bucket depletion.

title: Audit Machine Memory Pressure and Process Table
brief: Run a system resource audit script in python3 to check current swap usage, open file descriptor limits (`ulimit -n`), and top 3 memory-consuming local processes. Determine if local machine health supports launching a 4GB in-memory vector database instance. The final summary must detail swap space, file descriptor limits, top memory processes, and final launch permission verdict.
verify: The agent can verify ulimit and memory statistics using run_shell and ps utility commands.

title: Summarize Software Feature Specification
brief:
Read the following feature pitch:
"Our new logging service automatically captures uncaught exceptions, serializes the stack trace along with local environment variables, and pushes encrypted payloads to an internal storage bucket. It features configurable retention windows, automatic PII masking for email and SSN patterns, and real-time slack notifications for critical errors."
Rewrite this description into a concise 3-bullet technical summary suitable for API documentation. The final summary must contain the three bullet points capturing core functional features.
verify: The agent can run python3 line-count and word-count scripts to verify bullet structure.

title: Standardize Function Identifier Names
brief:
Take the following list of inconsistent function names:
- `get_user_by_id_from_db`
- `FetchAllOrders`
- `calc-tax-amount`
- `update_user_profile_data_in_database`
Rewrite all four names into idiomatic snake_case following standard RESTful naming conventions, ensuring names are concise and descriptive. The final summary must list the original function names alongside their standardized snake_case identifiers.
verify: The agent can run a python regex script verifying snake_case formatting across all target strings.

title: Translate Technical Spec to Plain Language
brief:
Translate the following architectural specification into non-technical prose for business stakeholders:
"The system implements an eventual consistency model using an asynchronous event bus. Writes are committed to a localized primary database, while read replicas consume published event streams to update cached projections, incurring an eventual latency window of up to 500ms."
Explain what this means for data visibility without using jargon. The final summary must provide the plain-language explanation.
verify: The agent can verify non-technical prose by checking for absence of technical terms (e.g. eventual consistency, pub/sub) via python3 string search.

title: Draft Error Message Taxonomy Document
brief: Draft standard user-facing error messages for three HTTP error states: 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, and 429 Too Many Requests. Ensure the tone is helpful, clear, and actionable, avoiding technical stack traces or hostile phrasing. The final summary must state the error code, technical cause, and exact draft user-facing error string for all three states.
verify: The agent can write a python script to check string length and sentence structure of messages.

title: Rewrite Complex API Reference Documentation
brief:
Rewrite the following verbose API description into a formal OpenAPI-style markdown endpoint specification:
"To create an invoice, send a POST request to /invoices with a JSON body. You must include customer_id (integer), items (array of objects with sku and quantity), and optional discount_code (string). If successful it returns 201 Created with the invoice ID and total amount."
Structure the document with clear section headers, parameter tables, and status codes. The final summary must contain the complete markdown document.
verify: The agent can write a python check verifying markdown section headers and table markup presence.

title: Analyze and Standardize Grammar and Voice
brief:
Examine the following mixed-voice user manual snippet:
"You should click the button. Then files are processed by the worker. We will send an email when completed. Do not close browser!"
Rewrite the entire paragraph into active, consistent imperative voice formatted as a step-by-step user guide. The final summary must present the revised step-by-step user guide.
verify: The agent can run python text analysis to check sentence start patterns and active verbs.

title: Recall Event Sequence from Incident Log
brief:

08:00:05 - Admin login from 192.168.1.50
08:02:12 - Database backup initiated
08:05:44 - Permission modified for user_id=104
08:12:00 - Database backup completed
08:15:30 - Admin logout
Recall and state what action occurred immediately after the database backup was initiated, citing the exact timestamp and log text. The final summary must state the timestamp and exact log line recalled from the incident log.
verify: The agent can write a python script to match and verify log lines by timestamp.

title: Retrieve Source Citation from Research Archive
brief:

[DocA] Smith et al. (2021): Transformer memory scales quadratically with sequence length N.
[DocB] Jones et al. (2023): Linear attention approximations reduce memory complexity to O(N).
[DocC] Patel et al. (2024): State space models achieve constant O(1) inference memory footprint.
Retrieve the document tag and exact author citation for the paper discussing state space models and O(1) memory. The final summary must state the document tag, author citation, and memory complexity value.
verify: The agent can parse the text string in python3 to confirm accurate extraction of DocC.

title: Reconstruct Timeline of Software Releases
brief:

- 2025-01-15: Release v1.0.0 (Initial Launch)
- 2025-03-10: Release v1.1.0 (Added OAuth2)
- 2025-02-01: Hotfix v1.0.1 (Patched SSL Vulnerability)

Reconstruct a chronological timeline of all releases from oldest to newest, citing release versions and dates. The final summary must present the ordered chronological release history table.
verify: The agent can verify date sorting logic using datetime parsing in python3.

title: Search Historical Commit Messages for Bug Fix
brief:
Search the following git log excerpt:
commit a1b2c3 - Fix: resolve memory leak in worker pool
commit d4e5f6 - Feat: implement Stripe webhook handler
commit g7h8i9 - Fix: repair race condition in session storage
commit j0k1l2 - Refactor: clean up database connections
Identify all commit hashes and messages that represent bug fixes (prefixed with "Fix:"). The final summary must list the matching commit hashes and their exact commit messages.
verify: The agent can write a python regex check searching for lines starting with commit and containing Fix:.

title: Audit Data Lineage across Multi-Stage Pipeline
brief:
Examine the recorded data pipeline provenance records:
Step 1 (09:00): Raw file `sales_raw.csv` ingested -> Table `staging_sales` (10,000 rows)
Step 2 (09:15): Transformation applied -> Table `fact_sales` (9,850 rows, 150 nulls dropped)
Step 3 (09:30): Aggregation -> Table `daily_summary` (30 rows)
Trace the data lineage for `daily_summary` back to its origin. Cite every intermediate table, row count delta, and timestamp. The final summary must detail the full step-by-step data lineage path.
verify: The agent can run python verification script to validate step sequence and row delta math.

title: Correlate Historical Outage Logs with Deployments
brief:
Examine two historical logs:
Deploy Log:
- 14:00 - Deploy v2.4.0
- 14:30 - Deploy v2.4.1
Incident Log:
- 14:12 - CPU spike 99% on node-02
- 14:35 - Error rate surge 5xx
Correlate each incident entry with the most recent prior deployment. The final summary must list each incident, its timestamp, and the preceding deployment version responsible.
verify: The agent can write a python script to compute time deltas and correlate events accurately.

title: Estimate Execution Duration for Sequential Tasks
brief:
A deployment pipeline consists of 4 sequential steps:
1. Dependency installation: 45 seconds
2. Code compilation: 120 seconds
3. Unit tests execution: 90 seconds
4. Container packaging: 60 seconds
Calculate total estimated duration in minutes and seconds, and estimate the project completion time if started at 10:00:00 AM. The final summary must state the total duration and projected completion timestamp.
verify: The agent can verify time math using datetime timedelta calculations in python3.

title: Forecast Storage Growth over 6 Months
brief: A database currently occupies 100 GB of storage and grows at a steady rate of 15 GB per month. Forecast total storage consumption after 6 months, and determine if storage will exceed a 200 GB volume limit. The final summary must report monthly projected totals, 6-month storage estimate, and volume limit status.
verify: The agent can write a simple linear growth script in python3 to check 6-month projection.

title: Decompose Application Migration into Milestones
brief: Decompose the goal "Migrate monolithic database to microservices" into a 4-phase milestone roadmap. For each phase, list key sequential steps, estimated duration in weeks, and primary technical risks. The final summary must present the structured 4-phase roadmap detailing steps, durations, and risk factors.
verify: The agent can run python string checks ensuring 4 phases are present with step and risk attributes.

title: Simulate What-If Scenario for Server Failure
brief: A web cluster has 4 identical nodes handling 1,000 requests per second total (250 req/sec per node). Node capacity is capped at 350 req/sec. Simulate a what-if scenario where 1 node suddenly fails. Calculate the new load per remaining node, compare against capacity limits, and forecast if cascading failure will occur. The final summary must state new load per node and cascading failure risk verdict.
verify: The agent can verify mathematical calculations via python script.

title: Model Monte Carlo Schedule Simulation
brief:
A software project has 3 sequential tasks with estimated durations (Best, Expected, Worst in days):
Task 1: (2, 4, 8)
Task 2: (3, 6, 12)
Task 3: (1, 3, 6)
Write a python simulation script in run_code using triangular distributions (1,000 iterations) to forecast the 50th and 90th percentile completion timelines in days. The final summary must report the calculated p50 and p90 projected completion timelines.
verify: The agent can execute python3 simulation script and assert output percentiles fall within expected range.

title: Simulate Queue Depletion under Spike Traffic
brief: An asynchronous task queue contains 5,000 items. Workers process 50 items per second. Simultaneously, a webhook surge adds 120 items per second for 30 seconds, after which incoming traffic drops to 0. Write a python script to simulate second-by-second queue depth, calculate peak queue size, and predict total time until queue drains to 0. The final summary must report peak queue depth and total drain time.
verify: The agent can run python simulation loop to verify exact peak depth and drain second.

title: Brainstorm Names for Microservice Project
brief: Brainstorm 5 creative, distinct project code-names for a new high-speed caching microservice. Draw analogies from physics, nature, and mythology. Ensure each name is unique and includes a 1-sentence rationale explaining the analogy. The final summary must list the 5 candidate names with their corresponding rationales.
verify: The agent can run python string length and line count checks on the summary.

title: Generate Alternative CLI Syntax Designs
brief: Propose 3 distinct command-line interface (CLI) flag design patterns for a data export tool (e.g. subcommands vs flags vs positional arguments). Show how a user would invoke an export of table `users` to JSON. The final summary must present the 3 CLI design proposals with example usage commands.
verify: The agent can verify 3 distinct proposals exist using python string splitting.

title: Synthesize Hybrid Caching Strategy Proposals
brief: Combine elements of In-Memory LRU Caching and Distributed Redis Caching to propose 3 novel hybrid caching architectural patterns. Describe how each pattern handles write-through vs write-back invalidation. The final summary must detail the 3 hybrid caching proposals and their invalidation mechanisms.
verify: The agent can write a python check verifying keyword presence across all 3 proposals.

title: Generate Analogies for Explaining Async Code
brief: Create 4 distinct real-world analogies (e.g. restaurant kitchen, postal service, assembly line, library) to explain asynchronous non-blocking event loops to junior developers. Each analogy must map terms (Event Loop, Call Stack, Callback Queue, Worker Thread) to real-world objects. The final summary must outline the 4 real-world analogies and their term mappings.
verify: The agent can verify presence of all 4 technical term mappings in each analogy via python script.

title: Propose Alternative Resilience Architectures
brief: A legacy monolithic service suffers from database connection exhaustion during traffic surges. Generate 4 creative architectural proposals (ranging from application-level patterns to infrastructure topology changes) to eliminate this bottleneck without rewriting core business logic. The final summary must present the 4 architectural proposals detailing mechanism and trade-offs.
verify: The agent can run python checks verifying 4 distinct proposals with trade-off sections.

title: Synthesize Cross-Domain Ideas for Data Privacy
brief: Draw principles from biological immune systems (e.g. self vs non-self recognition, memory cells, containment) to propose a novel software data privacy architecture. Define 4 specific system components inspired by immunology mechanisms. The final summary must describe the 4 immunology-inspired privacy components and their technical functions.
verify: The agent can verify 4 bio-inspired components exist using python text parsing.

title: Rank Security Vulnerabilities by Urgency
brief:
Examine the following 4 security findings:
1. SQL Injection in public login endpoint (CVSS 9.8)
2. Missing HSTS header on marketing site (CVSS 3.1)
3. Outdated minor dependency version in internal tool (CVSS 4.0)
4. Remote Code Execution in file upload worker (CVSS 9.8)
Rank these findings in order of remediation priority (1 highest to 4 lowest) considering CVSS score and attack vector. The final summary must list the prioritized ranking with brief rationale for each position.
verify: The agent can verify ranking order using python script logic.

title: Evaluate Cost-Benefit of Cloud DB Storage
brief:
Evaluate two cloud database options:
Option A: Managed PostgreSQL ($200/mo, 99.99% uptime, automated backups)
Option B: Self-hosted PostgreSQL on VM ($50/mo, 99.0% uptime, manual backups)
Compare cost vs operational overhead for a mission-critical billing service. Choose the optimal option and justify the decision. The final summary must state the selected option and detailed cost-benefit justification.
verify: The agent can run python check verifying decision selection and justification presence.

title: Score Feature Backlog using Weighted Matrix
brief:
Evaluate 3 product features (User Profiles, Dark Mode, Automated Invoicing) using a weighted scoring model:
- Revenue Impact (Weight 0.5, Score 1-10)
- User Demand (Weight 0.3, Score 1-10)
- Effort Required (Weight 0.2, Score 1-10, lower effort = higher score)
Assigned raw scores:
User Profiles: (3, 8, 5)
Dark Mode: (2, 9, 8)
Automated Invoicing: (9, 6, 4)
Calculate weighted total score for each feature and rank them. The final summary must present the weighted scores and prioritized backlog ranking.
verify: The agent can calculate exact floating-point weighted scores using python3 to verify ranking.

title: Conduct Trade-Off Analysis for Database Engine
brief: Perform a structured trade-off analysis between PostgreSQL (Relational) and MongoDB (Document) for building a real-time e-commerce analytics catalog. Evaluate across 4 criteria: Schema Flexibility, Query Complexity, ACID Compliance, and Scaling. Score each 1-5. The final summary must present the comparison matrix, total scores, and final recommendation.
verify: The agent can verify 4 criteria scores and matrix formatting using python script.

title: Prioritize Incident Response Actions under Crisis
brief:
During an ongoing outage, 4 alerts trigger simultaneously:
Alert A: Payment gateway failing (Impact: $500/min loss)
Alert B: Internal staging server offline (Impact: developer delay)
Alert C: Primary DB disk 94% full (Impact: total crash imminent in 10 min)
Alert D: Customer support widget slow (Impact: degraded UX)
Determine immediate triage sequence (Step 1 to 4), allocating limited 2-engineer capacity. The final summary must state the step-by-step triage sequence and engineer assignment rationale.
verify: The agent can run python script validating triage order priority logic.

title: Evaluate Technical Debt Remediation ROI
brief:
Assess 3 technical debt refactor candidates:
Debt 1: Refactor legacy auth (Cost: 2 weeks, Saves: 4 hrs/week bug fixing)
Debt 2: Migrate to TypeScript (Cost: 6 weeks, Saves: 2 hrs/week bug fixing)
Debt 3: Automate CI/CD pipeline (Cost: 1 week, Saves: 5 hrs/week deploy time)
Calculate payback period in weeks for each candidate and rank by Return on Investment (ROI). The final summary must present calculated payback periods and ROI ranking.
verify: The agent can execute python math checks to verify payback period calculations.

title: Draft Empathetic Customer Support Response
brief:
Read the following frustrated customer message:
"Your app crashed right when I was submitting my tax forms! Now I don't know if it went through and your phone line is busy! I need help NOW!"
Draft a calm, empathetic support reply that acknowledges their distress, provides immediate reassurance, and outlines clear next steps to verify submission. The final summary must contain the complete customer support draft reply.
verify: The agent can run python checks verifying empathy keywords and structured step guidance.

title: Deconstruct Intent from Vague User Request
brief:
Analyze the following short user request sent to an IT desk:
"The site is broken, fix it fast."
Deconstruct the underlying user intent, list 3 missing critical pieces of context required, and draft a polite, clarifying follow-up query. The final summary must detail the identified intent, missing context items, and draft follow-up query.
verify: The agent can verify 3 missing context items and follow-up query presence via python script.

title: Negotiate Scope Reduction with Stakeholder
brief: A product sponsor demands 5 major features delivered in 2 weeks, but engineering velocity supports only 3. Draft a diplomatic scope-negotiation email proposing a phased rollout (3 features in Phase 1, 2 features in Phase 2) that preserves stakeholder trust and explains capacity constraints constructively. The final summary must present the complete stakeholder negotiation email.
verify: The agent can run python checks to confirm presence of phased breakdown and polite tone indicators.

brief:
Read the technical post-mortem:
"A null pointer dereference in the auth handler caused worker crashes across the cluster due to missing error boundaries."
Adapt this explanation for two distinct audiences: (1) Executive Leadership (focusing on business impact and prevention) and (2) End Users (focusing on service status and security). The final summary must contain both tailored audience messages.
verify: The agent can verify presence of 2 distinct audience sections using python string matching.

title: Analyze Stakeholder Perspective in Architecture Dispute
brief:
Two team leads disagree on tech stack:
Lead A wants Rust (high performance, memory safety, steep learning curve).
Lead B wants Python (fast iteration, large talent pool, lower runtime speed).
Analyze the underlying goals, fears, and priorities of both Lead A and Lead B. Propose a collaborative compromise that addresses both perspectives. The final summary must detail the perspective analysis for both leads and the proposed compromise.
verify: The agent can write a python check verifying perspective analysis for both Lead A and Lead B.

brief: Write an API deprecation notice to third-party developers announcing that `v1/payments` will be shut down in 90 days. The notice must acknowledge the disruption, detail migration paths to `v2/payments`, offer developer support office hours, and maintain a respectful, partner-oriented tone. The final summary must present the complete deprecation announcement text.
verify: The agent can verify inclusion of timeline (90 days), migration path, and support details via python script.

- `src/index.js`
- `src/components/Header.js`
- `src/components/Footer.js`
- `public/favicon.ico`
- `package.json`
Construct an ASCII directory tree diagram representing this file hierarchy accurately. The final summary must contain the complete ASCII directory tree.

brief:

Box 2: (700, 550, 150, 100)
Box 3: (0, 0, 800, 600)

Determine which boxes fit entirely inside the canvas bounds and which overflow. The final summary must list each box ID and its containment status.
verify: The agent can run python coordinate geometry checks to verify bounds.

brief:
Examine service communication links:
- Service A calls Service B and Service C
- Service B calls Service D
- Service C calls Service D and Service E
Construct a directed graph adjacency matrix and identify critical path depth from Service A to Service E. The final summary must present the adjacency matrix and longest path depth count.
verify: The agent can write a python graph traversal script to verify adjacency matrix and depth.

brief:

- `orders.user_id` -> `users.id`
- `order_items.order_id` -> `orders.id`
- `order_items.product_id` -> `products.id`
- `payments.order_id` -> `orders.id`
Map the relational schema hierarchy starting from primary entity `users`. Identify root tables and leaf tables. The final summary must list the hierarchy depth, root tables, and leaf tables.
verify: The agent can verify graph roots and leaves using networkx or custom python dict logic.

title: Optimize Rack Server Slot Allocation Geometry
brief:
A server rack has 10 contiguous 1U slots (slot 1 to 10). Allocate 3 multi-U servers:
Server A (3U), Server B (2U), Server C (4U).
Slots 4 and 5 are damaged and unusable. Write a python placement script using run_code to find valid non-overlapping contiguous slot assignments for all 3 servers. The final summary must report the exact slot assignment mapping for Servers A, B, and C.
verify: The agent can run python placement validation script to ensure no overlap and valid slot bounds.

title: Detect Circular Dependencies in Module Import Graph
brief:
Examine module imports:
- `auth.js` imports `user.js` and `logger.js`
- `user.js` imports `db.js` and `config.js`
- `db.js` imports `logger.js` and `auth.js`
- `config.js` imports `env.js`
Build an import dependency graph in python3, detect any circular dependency loops, and list the exact cycle path. The final summary must state whether cycles exist and list the detected circular import path.
verify: The agent can execute a python cycle detection algorithm (DFS) to verify detected cycle.

title: J0
verify: A python check can recompute the group means from the block and confirm the named winner.

title: J1
brief:
Which gate has the strongest average?

W-00,upper,12.4,ok
W-01,upper,14.1,ok
W-02,lower,16.1,ok
W-03,lower,17.8,bad
W-04,mid,11.7,ok
W-05,mid,13.4,ok

Only rows marked ok count. Average the readings per gate, then name the winner and give its average to three decimals.
verify: Rerun the averaging by hand for each label; the largest should match what was reported.

title: J2
brief:

  finch    |    9.0 | ok
  crake    |    9.9 | ok
  crake    |   11.6 | bad
  teal     |    6.8 | ok

title: J3
brief: Cellar readings follow: [C-0] merlot=22.5 state=ok; [C-1] merlot=24.2 state=ok; [C-2] gamay=20.1 state=ok; [C-3] gamay=21.8 state=bad; [C-4] syrah=27.0 state=ok; [C-5] syrah=28.7 state=ok.
